Subject: ACME pilot: GPU sourcing & contingency plan

Team —

Quick sync request on sizing and contingency for the AcmeAI pilot (deal ACME-PIPE-2027-0421). Samir shared the attached pipeline snapshot — short pilot expected to ramp in June with an early-production window in August if the pilot metrics look good. Two asks:

1) Can infra confirm how many dedicated GPU slots (NVIDIA A800 equiv) we can commit for a 3-month pilot with a 30% burst allowance? If we cannot guarantee dedicated, what is the fallback (mixed dedicated + shared burst, or burst-only)?

2) Finance — need a run-rate estimate for the proposal (monthly committed cost + estimated burst spend) to present in the customer review on 5/27.

Notes from Samir (cc'd): they expect a conv-rate to dedicated within 12 weeks if latency and cost match their targets. We should build a conservative runway and a contingency route for capacity shortfall.

I've attached the pipeline summary Samir sent and a quick proposed burst allocation PDF. Please reply with numbers by EOD Wednesday so I can fold into the deck for Friday's review.

Thanks —

Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ACME pilot: GPU sourcing & contingency plan

Marissa —

Thanks for the context and the attach. Quick read-through and preliminary sizing below (will validate with ops tooling this afternoon):

- Conservative committed: 8 slots (A800 equiv) for 3 months (blocks the kernel pools required for low-latency chat workloads).
- Burst capacity: +30% -> additional 3 slots usable on top of committed across multi-tenant pools (best-effort latency).
- Fallback: If we can't sustain dedicated physical reservation for all 8 slots in the requested region, propose a hybrid: 5 committed + 6 burst (burst routed to compatible model-quant variants).

Operational caveats:
- KV cache warmup for chat sessions will add token pressure during ramp; recommend prefix-caching strategy and pre-warmed workers for the first 2 weeks of the pilot.
- If Acme requires strict isolation (no multi-tenant on burst), we need advanced notice; that will materially increase cost and lead time.

I'm running a quick capacity simulation now and will post the detailed numbers (+per-token forecast) by EOD.

Karthik
Director, Solutions & Capacity Planning | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Shah <samir@acmeai.com>, Priya Anand <priya@acmeai.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ACME pilot: GPU sourcing & contingency plan

Folks —

Thanks. From Finance perspective, we need two clear budget figures for Friday's customer review: (A) committed monthly cost (3-month term) and (B) conservative estimate for monthly burst / overage. Karthik's numbers are a good start; to convert to $ we need: committed slot price (monthly), expected average token throughput per slot, and estimated burst utilization percentage by week.

Prelim assumptions I will use unless someone flags otherwise:
- committed slot price: $14,500 / slot / month (region US-WEST)
- estimated average burst utilization: 18% of total pilot token consumption (conservative)
- billing model: committed discounted rate + overage billed at on-demand slot equivalent

If we go with Karthik's hybrid fallback (5 committed + 6 burst), monthly committed cost = $72,500; expected burst spend ~= $19k/month under the 18% assumption. I'll formalize and provide a line-item that includes amortized cache optimization credits if we enable prefix caching (small discount).

Question for Ben/Logan: do we have a hard constraint on mixed tenancy for burst slots for this customer? If burst can be multi-tenant, the numbers above hold. If they require single-tenant burst, send me the single-tenant slot premium and lead time so I can re-run the estimate.

Laura Bennett
Finance Partner, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
laura@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 16:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ACME pilot: GPU sourcing & contingency plan

Thanks all — helpful. Action items and next steps: 

- Karthik: please upload the capacity simulation CSV and per-token forecast to the linked sheet by EOD tomorrow. Link: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1AcmExAMPLElink 
- Ben/Logan: confirm tenancy constraint for burst and, if single-tenant is required, provide premium and earliest availability (ETA) by Thursday COB.
- Laura: finalize the two-line budget (committed + burst) with the assumptions called out; I will include in the customer review deck.
- Samir (Acme): could you confirm whether isolation on burst is a hard requirement for the pilot or a nice-to-have? A quick reply helps us lock pricing.

I'll book a 30-min pre-review on Thursday 5/27 10:00 AM PT to run through the deck unless anyone objects. Calendar invite to follow.
